output.brief: The rise in cancellations is mainly a Quillbook connector problem, not a price problem. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices: 58,300 across 1,212 of the 1,900 Quillbook accounts. 34% of those accounts have cancelled, against 8% of Quillbook accounts with no failures. Churn among Quillbook-connected accounts went from about 2% to about 6%, and it is the same for repriced and price-locked Founders accounts. Accounts with no connector, about 7,200, barely moved (1.8% to 1.9%) whether repriced or not, and that holds in every seat band. The seat-band pattern in the finance analysis appears because larger accounts are more likely to use Quillbook. Price complaints in exit surveys are probably partly a stated reason for a deeper problem. Tallymarsh changes are small and within normal variation, though its log is unreviewed. Recommendation: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority (3–4 weeks), and contact all affected accounts, including those who have cancelled, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold, since it has kept 3,870 duplicates out of customers' books. Do not roll back the price now, and do not start the Tallymarsh rebuild; instead, review the Tallymarsh log first. Also consider support triage so that sync issues are not treated as Sev-3.
